To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fourfold pattern is robust under a pricing procedure, and that the fourfold is not robust under a choice procedure.

(1) risk aversion is not universal; (2) risk attitudes depend on both probability and outcome magnitude, and are thus best represented by a fourfold pattern; (3) the pattern is robust to elicitation procedure, and (4) the price elicitation procedure yields a more robust fourfold pattern than choice.
(a) the fourfold pattern holds for price-based elicitation, but not for choice-based elicitation and (b) the price-based elicitation procedure is cognitively more demanding.
